en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Greatly Majestic and Miraculous Vajrayakṣa Krodharāja Śāntika,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi Gaganagañja surveyed the great bodhisattvas,
devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings within the celestial palace,
and rose from his seat, baring his right shoulder.
He addressed Śākyamuni Buddha, saying:
"In the distant past, during immeasurable koṭis of great kalpas,
for the sake of seeking the Dharma..."
As we transmigrate through the vessel-world (*bhājana-loka*),
there are many such as King Pāpīyas who cause us to greatly regress from the Buddha-dharma.
We pray only that the Bhagavat [will protect us].
He requested to hear the exposition of the mantra of great majestic power and efficacy that manifests through expedient bodies.
The Buddha asked, "What expedient body do you wish to manifest?
He replied, "I pray that you will manifest the form of the Great Holy Yakṣa Vajra."
The Buddhas of the past have already appeared;
the Buddhas of the present appear now;
the Buddhas of the future shall appear.
I am now neither of the past, nor of the present, nor of the future.
Manifesting the wrathful form of my own mind’s samādhi,
I shall protect the Buddha-dharma and compassionately regard all sentient beings.

The Buddha said, "Excellent! Great Sage, you who wish to protect and uphold the Buddha-dharma and take pity on sentient beings, you may well manifest skillful means and proclaim this mantra of great spiritual efficacy.
I shall empower and sustain you with my protective mindfulness."
As they all together recited the mantra to compassionately protect and uphold [the practitioner],
he immediately, without rising from his seat,
manifested as a three-faced, six-armed, greatly majestic and wrathful deity with a poisonous form.
Adorned with necklaces of the seven precious jewels,
their bodies were immense, and flames blazed from every part of their bodies like the fierce and terrifying smoke and fire at the end of an eon.
Gazing in the four directions like the lion-king elephant, valiant and courageous;
the practitioner who first maintains the mantra should hold the *śikhā* (topknot) as a bell-fist at the level of the breasts.
Using the *kha* syllable, one forms the sword-binding mudrā and places it upon the knees.
Using the *ja* syllable together with the first *aḥ*, one makes a fist and draws it inward;
using the second *vaṃ* together with the *aḥ*, one gazes with the *kha*.
The "feather" (yu) gesture consists of both hands forming the "majestic phoenix crushing rice" (fengwei posu) posture.
Together with the third syllable *aḥ*, one stops below and observes above while striking the beat to produce sound.
Together with the fourth syllable *gan*, one draws out the two feathers and rotates them.
Reciting "Paṭa" five times, alternate between śamatha and vipaśyanā three times up and down; encircle the body with the fist,

place it upon the crown of the head, rotate it three times to the left to perform the ritual of expulsion (*vidhūnana*), and rotate it three times to the right to perform the ritual of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
Thereafter, he pressed each of the four seals together,
with eyes glaring and mouth contorted in rage;
his body trembling with intense fear, he recited the vidyā-mantra as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām | Arkaya vinaya aḥ | Vīcika vajrāṇe | Sṭhira vaṃ aḥ | Dharma sarvadharmagati vigalini ||
ĀṂ VIKARIṆE ŚATRŪṂ HŪṂ AḤ KṚI KṚI GĀMINI GĀMINI GAGĀMINI GAṂ UCU MĀRANI ŚATRŪṂ HŪṂ.
Vajra vajra (13) taggini (14) taggini (15) svāhā (16) svāhā (17) hūṃ phaṭ (18). At that time, the Buddha spoke this mantra.
The trichiliocosm shook in six ways;
the palaces inhabited by the hosts of Maheśvara and other Great Sovereign Lords all became disarrayed and unstable.
All have gathered here like clouds to pay homage to the Yakṣa Vajra;
we pray that the Great Powerful Honored One will take pity on us and grant us fearlessness, peace, and majestic power.
The Yakṣa King addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Regarding these Māras and their like, what is it that they worry about and distress them? What do they desire?"
The Buddha said, "I shall for a time allow these pitiable ones to obtain happiness.
Having thus granted their request,
the King of Māras immediately addressed the Wrathful King, saying:
We shall all together exert our supernatural powers to protect the Buddha-dharma, and each shall withdraw and disperse.
If there are evil persons who harbor enmity toward virtuous people and cause them disturbance and affliction,
the Dharma Master should paint an image of the Miraculous Wrathful King, according to his preference for its size, whether large or small.
Construct a triangular altar facing the direction where the person resides.
With a malicious intent, recite the aforementioned mantra of great spiritual efficacy twenty-one times during each of the three periods of the day.
When three days have passed,
the deceased person's family and kin will have perished with no survivors remaining.
If one wishes to restore them to life, one should take the root of a lotus flower and grind it into a powder.
By reciting the Great Compassion Samādhi Mantra one hundred and eight times for a full day and night without food or drink,
the evil person and their kinsmen will immediately revive.
Raising one’s faith and reverence for the Buddha-dharma,
join the two hands in fists and bend the index fingers;
form a hollow opening with them and draw it away.
One should give rise to great compassion. The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ gajapalaṣṭhu huṃ svāhā*. If one wishes to obtain the great spiritual efficacy of the Buddha-dharma, [one should recite this].
First, construct a square altar measuring four cubits before the image.
Place a large vessel of white copper in the center of the altar and fill it completely with scented water.
From the first day of the month until the fifteenth,
burn incense, scatter flowers, and pay homage with sincere devotion while reciting the Great Mantra of Efficacious Response.
Day and night, without interruption, he never sleeps;
his vigor is entirely firm and steadfast,
and he neither rests nor halts.
Without interruption for fifteen days,
one completes one hundred thousand recitations;
the Yakṣa King will then manifest his own form to bestow empowerment upon the practitioner.
Because one immediately recollects and takes pity upon sentient beings,
manifesting an exquisite form,
why would the awakening of both worlds not be accomplished?
Thereupon, those who were filled with fear and were empowered by this wrathful deity—
including evil persons, malevolent māras, wicked beasts, and even those employing curses,
sorcery, and spells, as well as goblins, imps, and malevolent spirits— [were subdued].
If those who give rise to evil intentions, desiring to harass and harm the practitioner,
approach the practitioner’s dwelling from near or far,
they will be killed by their own hands along the way.
This divine efficacy extends for thirty *li* around,
ensuring that no obstacles exist.
Furthermore, it is so that the Vajra Yakṣa may exercise his power of subduing through bestowal.
Because the root great-heart mantra of the Great Fierce Wrathful King (Mahābhairava-rāja) is an extremely secret mantra-seal,
it is not presented here as a ritual manual;
it is found in a separate fascicle.
One should draw near to the ācārya and serve him so as to practice and learn;
because it is extremely secret, when reciting this mantra, [one must do so].
All the hosts of Māras and spirits shall find no peace, being struck with terror;
this shall be no different from a mantra of great efficacy.
The Distinction of Mantra and Seal:
If one wishes to practice this mantra,
it should be done according to the *Āryācala-sādhana-vidhi*.
As for the ritual procedure: first, place the right knee on the ground and,
with a sincere heart, take refuge in all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
repenting of the karmic obstacles of sin from beginningless birth and death.
I rejoice in all the roots of goodness accumulated by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
I entreat all the Tathāgatas and the assembly of noble ones to give rise to the bodhicitta and make offerings to all Buddhas. The mantra for this entreaty is as follows:
Oṃ vajrayakṣa yattadākarṣaya vidhvaṃsaya hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. The mantra for bathing the image is as follows:
Oṃ hūṃ sarvanīya haṃ. The mantra for the argha (water offering) is:
Oṃ aparādhye hūṃ. The mantra for the seat is: Oṃ āsana... [etc.]
Oṃ vikaraṇi svāhā. The mantra for putting on clothes and ornaments is:
Oṃ kuṇi kuṇi sa-kuṇiye īmukhaṃ. The mantra for incense, flowers, lamps, and ointments is: [as above].
Oṃ maṇināgagaṇa samasama kūṭe svāhā. The Vajra-yakṣa praised him, saying:
"Vajra-aitula yakṣa vajra-tiṣṇi vīrili hani hani vajra mahāyakṣa yakṣa pāṇigāṇiya svāhā. May [the deity] quickly give rise to joy and a delighted mind.
One may recite this verse of praise:

Excellent, excellent, O Yakṣa! You who have compassion for sentient beings such as ourselves, you who are peerless and manifest as a being among all creatures—what is it that brings peace, and what is it that causes affliction?
The mantra for consecrating the rosary is:
Oṃ vajra-jvālini. The mantra for sending forth [the offerings] is:
Oṃ vikṣaya hūṃ phaṭ. These are the mantras for the ten types of offerings, praises, and so forth, as previously described.
All should hold a three-pronged vajra.
With both hands grasping the prongs at the heart, one should recite each mantra while visualizing that majestic power flows forth from them.
Holding the vajra-club, the mantra is:
Oṃ saṃbhavajra heḍi vi-bha-vajra aḥ. If one wishes to be liberated from all obstacles and difficulties.
Combine the two *liang* of pill medicine;
holding each portion in the left and right palms respectively,
squat down and recite the Great Efficacious Mantra seven times.
If one applies this empowered substance to the back,
one will be instantly liberated from all obstacles, difficulties, disputes, untimely deaths, and short lifespans. Furthermore,
if one wishes to swiftly slay an evil person:
Place the portrait of the person, along with their name, upon the subjugation mandala.
At its initial corner, carve a bamboo peg and drive it through the center of the abdomen.
Recite the mantra of great efficacy.
With a heart of sudden rage,
uttering the incantation one hundred and eight times,
striking once for each repetition, the victim shall die immediately.
Furthermore, if one wishes to swiftly bind an evil person and cause them to return to the Buddha-way,
one should recite the Great Dharani three times with a malevolent mind,
take a black stone, and together with it, utter "Phaṭ! at the end.
If one turns the wings inward, they will naturally become bound.
Furthermore, if one wishes to release them,
recite the Great Compassion Samaya-mantra three times.
Having immediately regained his original mind, he said:
"From this day forward, I take refuge in the Buddha-way;
henceforth, I shall never again give rise to wrong views or unwholesome thoughts."
Furthermore, if one desires to obtain a beautiful woman for oneself or to cause another to obtain one,
one should write the name of the beautiful woman on pine bark,
tie it before the image, and recite the Great Compassion Samādhi Mantra.
Recite this seven times as an announcement to the King of Fierce Wrath.
In this manner, maintain focused mindfulness during the three periods of each day and announce it to the King of Fierce Wrath out of his compassionate regard.
With the mind of a noble woman of his own station,
he did not allow any other thought to arise; having come forth from his palace and residence,
he was deeply attached to the lady.
They have no other thoughts;
rather, it is that another’s wife is not one’s own husband,
and the husband grows weary of the wife while the wife grows weary of the husband.
With single-minded devotion, he took refuge in his later wife;
together they constantly gave rise to the bodhicitta and perpetually taught and transformed the lady.
Furthermore, if one desires to obtain an official position,
one should burn incense with a sincere heart before the image and present various kinds of offerings.
For three days and three nights, or even for seven days and seven nights,
one may recite the mantra of the Great Compassionate Samādhi and offer prayers.
When not a single one of one's aspirations fails to be accomplished,
one should perform the rite of augmentation (puṣṭi).
This is for the time when one practices solely for the sake of personal accomplishment.
Having followed the recollection and gazed toward the directions,
and having minutely indicated the directions as in the ritual procedure for the homa altar,
one who wishes to exit the maṇḍala should recite this mantra.
The mantra for dismissing the assembly of noble ones is:
Oṃ vajrayakṣa tiṣṭha tiṣṭha hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ. When performing these various rites of formidable power and wrathful activity, [recite this].
May all Maras and adversaries be subdued and protected;
may you uphold the Buddha-dharma.
Therefore, when the practitioner cultivates [this practice],...
Be careful not to give rise to evil thoughts that repeatedly harm others.
A person of wisdom who well understands this secret path must not recite the mantra while distracted.
Except for those who are gentle, mild, and patient,
reaching the age of forty and thus attaining self-compliance and compliance with others;
if a wise person acts like a child while practicing recitation, they shall not attain the path of liberation.
This involves the grave fault of harming oneself and others.
A practitioner should generally possess compassion and benefit the entire realm of sentient beings;
then, upon leaving the hall, they may read and recite the Mahāyāna sūtras as they please.
The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of Vajrayakṣa, Abiding on the Stage of Non-Retrogression.
